items.summary: A self-hosted personal agent: web research, a live browser you can watch and take over, reminders and background checks, goals broken into plans, and memory stored as readable plain-text files. It asks for approval before spending, sending or submitting anything. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, needs no account, keeps state in PostgreSQL, and starts with one Docker Compose command. Apache-2.0; bring your own OpenAI API key.
items.title: Amuse: Replit's self-hosted personal agent that runs only on your own computer, bound to localhost (released Nov 19)

items.summary: A free, open-source desktop agent built for beginners: download it, paste in your own API key, and it builds websites, does research and writes code, asking for approval before consequential actions. Chats, memory and API keys stay on your machine. It supports Markdown skills, Discord chat and one-click MCP connections to 145 services, with installers for Windows, macOS and Linux. MIT licensed.
items.title: RedCat: a beginner-first open-source desktop agent that runs locally and asks before consequential actions (Show HN, Nov 18)
